name: Krista Loughton
office: Council (also seeking CRD Director — three CRD Director seats on the Victoria ballot)

doors.label: Tax cap
doors.sentence: Voted YES on the 2026 budget (7.28% overall / 9.34% residential): "OPPOSED (3): Councillor Gardiner, Councillor Hammond, and Councillor Kim / CARRIED (6 to 3)", all nine present. In 2023 she moved the motion that raised that year's increase: "allocate an additional $500,000 to the 2023 City budget, bringing the property tax increase to approximately 6.3%". No cap, formula or glide path anywhere in 2026. "Fairer taxes" is regional police cost-sharing, scored on row 33.

doors.label: Downtown order
doors.sentence: "Continue OUR DWTN for cleanliness and safety, to support arts, culture and events, and increase foot traffic to local shops." No Public Order Team, no unified command, no 6am–10pm bylaw hours, and no 2026 statement of any kind on bylaw enforcement. Record on the same door: she moved the 2023 and 2024 motions funding the VicPD Downtown Late Night Task Force and downtown foot patrol (row 6).

doors.label: Housing
doors.sentence: "Continue to champion affordable housing by prioritizing non-profit and workforce housing to ensure renters, families, and seniors can continue to live in Victoria." Her record page claims "Victoria has surpassed provincial housing targets, approved approximately 9,000 new homes (50% rental and 20% affordable)". No unit target of her own and no 25/20/15 composition split. Counterweight in the same window: Times Colonist, "Victoria falls below target for medium and low-income housing".

doors.label: Written program
doors.sentence: Authorized 2026 site ("Authorized by Charlene Bart, financial agent") with a three-pillar priorities page and a delivered-record page. Not costed, no targets, no dates. Internal contradiction: the home page and the survey page both say "Councillor Loughton will be using your vital feedback to inform her 2026 campaign platform", while /priorities presents a settled platform with no provisional caveat. Her VoteMate 2026 profile is blank ("hasn't uploaded a profile yet") and the X account her own footer links to returns 404.

cells.quote: Victoria has surpassed provincial housing targets, approved approximately 9,000 new homes (50% rental and 20% affordable), and adopted the new OCP to guide future growth".
cells.why: Commits (action taken) with a stated composition mix, plus the forward line "Continue to champion affordable housing by prioritizing non-profit and workforce housing". Comparable instrument: a composition claim and the Affordable Rental Housing Revitalization Tax Exemption ("10% of units renting at 30% of median income — about $1,400 instead of $2,100 for a new one-bedroom"), not M6's competitive land disposition or 25/20/15 targets. Capped below Close by a sourced miss on the same measure: Times Colonist, 21 Jun 2026, "Victoria falls below target for medium and low-income housing", against her own page's "surpassed provincial housing targets". Record, matching, not a second mark: named YES on Missing Middle 26 Jan 2023.

cells.quote: The City's Housing Reserve Fund invested $5.4 million to support 475 new homes at sites like 926–930 Pandora, Wellness House, and Village on the Green.
cells.why: A City capital fund deployed to non-market projects, claimed on her record page. Not scored: it is not a land bank, there is no parcel-level public inventory, no strategic acquisition fund, no competitive disposition scored on speed and design, and no right-of-first-refusal for non-profit or Indigenous housing partners. Does not contradict a 2026 promise, so 📋, not a mark.

cells.quote: The Fast Track for Affordable Housing program helped speed up the application processing time to deliver these projects faster.
cells.why: Commits (action taken); same page claims the City "sped up approvals (especially for non-market and rental housing)". Comparable instrument: Fast Track is a tenure-based priority stream, which is one of M7's own listed instruments. Not Aligned: no published permit times by category, no service standard, no quarterly variance report, no one-stop centre, no AI pre-screening — and M7's flagship claim is the publication, which she has never made. Absence of a benchmark is Record, not a cap, so Close stands.

cells.quote: Moved By Councillor Loughton / Seconded By Councillor Thompson — "a.
cells.why: For one time only, the Downtown Late Night Task Force, up to $220,000 … b. A VicPD downtown foot patrol project to add increased police presence to the downtown core, at $35,200" (CARRIED 7 to 2, 6 Apr 2023). She moved the same task force again on 29 Jan 2024 ($280,000). Not scored: a late-night police task force is not M26's unified operation — no VicPD + Bylaw + Public Works + Outreach single command, no 8 AM briefing, no single field supervisor, no co-located desk, no weekly DPOT dashboard. The foot patrol instrument is scored once, on row 12. Does not contradict a 2026 promise.

cells.quote: Mental health outreach expanded this term through the Co-Response Team, a partnership between Island Health and VicPD, and Crisis Response, Community Led (CRCL), a civilian-led mobile team providing trauma-informed care during mental health crises.
cells.why: Commits (action taken; "Councillor Loughton led advocacy work for the Province to better align outreach teams with housing pathways and recovery supports"). Comparable instrument: a civilian-led mobile crisis team exists and she advocates for it, but there are no published dispatch criteria agreed with VicPD, Fire, BCEHS and Island Health, and no published diversion figure, and it is not dispatched from an M26 co-located board she does not have. Context, her own named 2026 motion, not a second mark: co-author with Coun. Hammond of "Emergency Response to the Medetomidine Crisis" (30 Jul 2026) asking the Province and Island Health for "Dedicated resources for frontline outreach" and "Immediate, on-demand pathways to treatment and recovery services" — M26b's own advocacy-at-zero-cost fallback.

cells.quote: FLAG from pass 1 now resolved from the official record.
cells.why: 18 Jul 2024, main motion as amended: "direct the City Manager … to put an end to illegal daytime temporary sheltering in Victoria parks and on city streets, sidewalks and boulevards" — "OPPOSED (1): Councillor Kim / CARRIED (8 to 1)", nine present, so Loughton voted yes. Balancing fact from the same meeting: she was among the four who supported softening the wording to "continue to try to put an end to" — "OPPOSED (5): Mayor Alto, Councillor Coleman, Councillor Dell, Councillor Gardiner, and Councillor Hammond / DEFEATED (4 to 5)". Continuity in 2026: "I have been doing everything I can this term to get people moved indoors, because tents are not a solution to homelessness." Not scored: this is a 2024 action with no 2026 bylaw-enforcement promise to contradict.

cells.what: drug-use buffer (City: list + bylaw/DPOT + VicPD/CDSA; not City seizure)
cells.quote: 2 Jul 2026: the motion to close the supervised consumption site at The Harbour failed with only Coun.
cells.why: Gardiner in favour — she did not support closure. Reported speech, not a quote, so not scored as a sentence: "It's not about what's happening inside The Harbour, it's about what's happening outside, said Coun. Krista Loughton". Not scored: buffer zones, a protected list of child-focused spaces, and CDSA coordination do not appear. Does not contradict a 2026 promise.

cells.quote: Led the creation of the Housing Relocation Program which moved 75+ people indoors, and out of encampments in Stadacona, Topaz, Irving and Vic West parks — and the work is ongoing throughout the city.
cells.why: Commits, same instrument on two of the four: M35 capacity-first — "people who were staying at city parks that were subsequently closed to overnight camping were offered housing through a city-funded team before the parks were closed to camping. To date, that team has housed more than 70 people" is M35's "build capacity first, then enforce, and never move people to nowhere", verbatim in substance; M36 visible presence — "downtown foot patrols (Councillor Loughton led reviving this with VicPD's Chief Constable in early 2023)". Cluster misses M37 all-night lighting entirely and has no written same-day removal protocol (M34). Distinct sentence from Positive Flow, which is row 23; distinct from the Late Night Task Force, which is row 6.

cells.what: tax glide path (capped on the residential rate)
cells.quote: Five Year Financial Plan Bylaw 26-040, 7 May 2026: "OPPOSED (3): Councillor Gardiner, Councillor Hammond, and Councillor Kim / CARRIED (6 to 3)" — nine present, so a Loughton YES on 7.28% overall and 9.34% residential.
cells.why: Disagrees with a capped residential glide path. Compounding action: on 6 Apr 2023 she moved "allocate an additional $500,000 to the 2023 City budget, bringing the property tax increase to approximately 6.3%", and voted to defeat the Coleman/Gardiner amendment that would have funded it from contingency instead of a tax increase. Context, same debate, not a second mark: she voted "with a heavy heart" — "The public must understand the staggering cost of our current direction. We are paying a crisis premium for services that manage the symptoms of an issue rather than solving the cause." 2026 "fairer taxes" is scored on row 33.

cells.quote: 3 Mar 2026, part 1 of the mayor's motion: "Approve reducing the 2026 debt reduction allocation to zero" — "OPPOSED (3): Councillor Kim, Councillor Caradonna, Councillor Gardiner / CARRIED (6 to 3)", nine present, ratified identically 12 Mar 2026.
cells.why: The financial plan shows the zeroed line as $2,000,000, and $5,500,000 of the $5,700,000 recovered was directed "to reduce the property tax increase". Why this is Record and not Opposed: M66c makes the scheduled debt-reduction contribution unavailable as a balancing item absent a 6-of-9 supermajority with a published rationale — this vote was 6 of 9 in open session, so it clears M66c's own override rather than breaching it. Not scored: no over-collection refund rule, no published debt ceiling, no quarterly debt metrics. She is not named; the yes is derived from a complete attendance list and a named opposed list.

cells.quote: Hold all CRD municipalities accountable to host their fair share of supportive services for the homeless. Victoria cannot continue to carry the load alone.
cells.why: Commits, and backed by a sourced 2026 instrument: her 12 Feb 2026 motion asked staff "to work with BC Housing and the Capital Regional District to develop a regional positive transfer system for supportive housing", and the 5 Feb 2026 direction was "to work with the CRD, BC Housing, and other partners in developing a potential cost shared STEP-like positive flow pilot" (CARRIED UNANIMOUSLY). Comparable, not same: no quarterly downloading ledger, no twice-yearly UBCM/FCM resolutions, and no published refusal threshold naming what Victoria will not assume without indexed funding — which is precisely the instrument her own "cannot carry the load alone" argument needs. Running for CRD Director is office-seeking, not a source; the sentence and the motions are.

cells.what: CRD cost and the Goldstream plant
business, downtown, one mandate not a new office
cells.quote: Work with the business community to develop an economic development plan and retail strategy.
cells.why: Commits. Comparable instrument for M73d, a Council-adopted Strategic Economic Plan, reinforced by "Pragmatic support for downtown businesses, recognizing that a thriving downtown benefits the entire region." Not Aligned: no storefront vacancy number (11% → 5%), no quarterly vacancy report by block, no one-mandate-not-a-new-office construction, no Conference Centre target or net cost, no employment-lands inventory. OUR DWTN is scored on row 26; the non-profit grocery bullet is not a measure in this 55.

cells.what: capital threshold, short-stay parking (15-min grace; first-hour gated Year 2), permit fees
Host Nations Foundation. Topic never drops out of the 12. A dash is still allowed on M1–M5.
tenant protections, STR, indoor heat (M9c struck; 26°C gated)
cells.quote: I think it's really important that we do everything we can to keep temperatures under 26 degrees in rental buildings. And based on the last heat dome and the loss of life, we just need to do everything we can.
cells.why: Commits, same instrument and same number as M64: the 14 May 2026 motion directs staff to "Explore the tools available for the City to adopt a bylaw, or modify an existing bylaw, that restricts landlords from prohibiting cooling equipment, and/or requires existing rental units to have a heat pump, or other cooling equipment or passive means, that prevents at least one room of the unit from exceeding the standard recommendation of 26 C (79 F)" — M64's exact two-step sequence and its Standards-of-Maintenance-Bylaw hook. She is named among the eight who refused to postpone it ("OPPOSED (8): … Councillor Loughton … / DEFEATED (1 to 8)"), and on 23 Jul 2026 she moved the carried passive-cooling amendment. Second same-instrument hit on M9: co-author, with Couns. Thompson and Caradonna, of "Increasing Protections for Victoria Renters" (28 May 2026, passed unanimously), asking staff to report on "the first year of the Tenant Protection During Redevelopment Bylaw and whether it may be necessary to strengthen it" and on "options to improve compliance with the Rental Property Standards of Maintenance Bylaw". Her quote: "Expanding tenant supports isn't just about stability; it is vital to homelessness prevention." Context, not a second mark: unanimous 3 Mar 2026 vote for "$100,000 to the Community Social Planning Council for its Rent Bank program". Cluster miss: M9b short-term rental licensing is absent entirely. Note for the Program, not a mark: the same motion asks staff to report on "rent control and vacancy control measures", which v1.10 declined as a provincial RTA file when M9c was dropped.

cells.quote: That Council direct staff to work with community and government partners as needed to set up a By Name List for the unsheltered homeless population in the City of Victoria and report on its status monthly to Council.
cells.why: Commits — she is the named author on the agenda ("From: Councillor Krista Loughton"), and the amended motion passed unanimously 30 Jul 2026. Her framing: "by name lists moves us from guessing how many people are experiencing homelessness once a year to knowing every individual by name in real time so we can connect them to the exact housing and support that they need." Comparable, not same: a real-time by-name list with monthly reporting is not M10's single digital portal with published point-based scoring, visible queue position and a no-outside-intervention rule. HIFIS entered by floor amendment, not in her written motion. Staff report back 3 Sep 2026.

cells.quote: Established the Positive Transfer Program which will free up 100 supportive housing spots to reduce visible homelessness.
cells.why: Commits, same instrument and same target. Same instrument: her own motion, minuted 15 Jan 2026 as "Council Member Motion: Positive Flow: Unlocking Supportive Housing and Shelter Spaces … requesting the City explore adopting a program similar to the Supporting Tenants, Enabling Pathways Program", directing staff to "Contact the City of Vancouver to request information and materials related to the STEP program model" and "Contact BC Housing and Island Health … to explore collaboration" — CARRIED UNANIMOUSLY. STEP is M11's own named instrument. Same target: her record page says Positive Flow "could free up an estimated 100 units of supportive housing for those still on the street in Victoria, cutting visible homelessness in half", which is M11's −50%. Funded: "allocate $200,000 toward a 'Positive Flow' housing initiative" carried 7 to 2 on 3 Mar 2026 and rode into the adopted financial plan. Her words: "It is critically important. It's the most important thing that this council will do for the rest of this term." Cluster miss, shown: no published quarterly count, no cost-per-placement, no returns-to-homelessness figure — M11's dollars-to-outcomes reporting is absent. Park relocation is row 12.

cells.what: childcare, doctors, youth (M13 school food is $0 → M13d)
cells.quote: The Allied Health Clinic opened this term and provides team-based care with family doctors and nurse practitioners.
cells.why: Commits (action taken, under her own 2022 promise heading "Work with the Province to increase access to family doctors and addiction treatment"). Neither instrument: no s.224 permissive tax exemption for not-for-profit clinics, no below-market lease of City space with bulk-billing conditions, no fast-track clinic permitting, no published net-new-practitioner figure. Cluster: childcare (M12, 500 spaces, 60-day permits) and the 18–25 cohort (M13c) are absent entirely. M13 school food is $0 and is not scored here.

cells.quote: 4 Apr 2024: main motion as amended asking the Mayor to write to SD61 "further requesting reinstatement of the Police School Liaison Officers" — "OPPOSED (4): Councillor Caradonna, Councillor Dell, Councillor Kim, and Councillor Thompson / CARRIED (5 to 4)", nine present, so a Loughton yes. Not scored: a letter to the board is not M13d's standing joint agreement with a published annual work plan, an annual joint public meeting, a joint-use facilities agreement, a safe-routes-to-school programme or a single named City contact. Does not contradict a 2026 promise; SD61 does not appear in her 2026 material at all.
The City's around the clock street-cleaning program clears litter, empties bins, power-washes sidewalks, and removes graffiti in public places.
cells.why: Commits (action taken), plus the forward line "Continue OUR DWTN for cleanliness and safety". Same instrument on M17 — around-the-clock sweeping and bin emptying in the downtown core is M17's extended-hours commitment — and on M18, "My Great Neighbourhood Grants also supported local initiatives", M18's own named vehicle. Not Aligned: no 90%-of-graffiti-in-48-hours published standard (M14) and no anti-rat or pest management plan (M16), and "Intense focus continues in hot spots" is not a service standard. One sentence, one measure: the /priorities OUR DWTN sentence is used here, not on rows 6, 18, 36 or 39.

cells.what: mobility + Vision Zero (M39 30 km/h struck; calming is M38)
cells.quote: Expanding the Bike and Roll network
cells.why: Commits (listed among "Major initiatives Councillor Loughton supported this term"), touching M41's protected-network family. Neither instrument at cluster level: it is a bare list item with no gap map, no km target and no capital line, and the rest of the cluster is empty — no adaptive signal control (M19), no E&N or Westshore rapid-transit endorsement or right-of-way protection (M22), no dangerous-intersection redesign programme (M38), no speed-enforcement site nomination (M40), no Vision Zero audit step (M42). M39 is struck and is not scored. The airport-express bullet is regional advocacy and sits on row 28.

cells.what: walking and transit the City controls
VicPD funding + regional review (convene-and-publish; no binding other force)
cells.quote: Fight for fairer taxes by advocating for regional cost-sharing on community safety and policing.
cells.why: Commits. Neither instrument: no renegotiated Esquimalt funding formula on service-consumption metrics, no four-year review cycle, no mediation route, and no time-boxed costed regional services review with published terms of reference and a published offer-and-refusal. FLAG from pass 1 now resolved: on 3 Mar 2026 she voted for cutting the VicPD ask from four new officers to two — "OPPOSED (4): Mayor Alto, Councillor Hammond, Councillor Gardiner, Councillor Coleman / CARRIED (5 to 4)", nine present. Victoria Buzz, single source, also names her as seconder: "Councillor Krista Loughton seconded Caradonna's motion". Shown as context, not a second mark and not a cap: cutting a headcount does not contradict a promise to advocate for regional cost-sharing, and the Program sets no VicPD headcount.

cells.what: safety dashboard, published enforcement record, crime target
cells.quote: Adopting the Community Safety & Wellbeing Plan
cells.why: Commits (action taken). Neither instrument: M31c keeps that same June 2025 plan but retrofits it into a performance contract — "Every major commitment restated with five mandatory fields: legal authority, responsible lead body, implementation timeline, measurable target, projected cost" plus a published implementation matrix and quarterly outcome reporting. She has the plan and none of the retrofit: no weekly safety dashboard (M31), no published enforcement record with uphold rates (M31b), no crime-reduction target (M32).

cells.quote: Investing in Hermann's Jazz Club
cells.why: Commits (action taken). Hermann's is the named trigger case for M46b, so the subject matches. Neither instrument: a single named investment is not M46b's designated list of cultural venues of city-wide significance, right-of-first-refusal on sale or lease termination, permissive tax exemption or lease-bridge fund. Cluster: "a full heritage program review and update is coming soon" is staff work with no commitment attached, and there is no design code, street-furniture standard or demolition-by-neglect position. Heritage-body seats on the City biography are a seat held, not a source.

cells.quote: Transforming parks with upgrades at Topaz, Stadacona, and an expanded dock at Banfield (with a potential new dock in the Gorge, stay tuned!)
cells.why: Commits (action taken). Neither instrument: no restored Parks horticulture operating budget, no Beacon Hill five-year restoration plan, no signature horticultural feature per neighbourhood, no free-seedling canopy programme (M49); no closing of the Songhees–Selkirk or Gorge walkway gaps (M47) — a dock is not a walkway; no heritage restoration incentive fund (M46); no extension of ornamental lighting to midnight (M48). Context: unanimous votes on 7 and 20 Nov 2025 restored the $75,000 Growing in the City grant stream that funds Get Growing, Victoria!, in which she is not named.

cells.what: culture, sport, and the arts funding floor
cells.quote: The award-winning OUR DWTN program brought markets, live music, and events to spaces such as Ship Point and Centennial Square.
cells.why: Commits (action taken). Same instrument as M51 — activating outdoor spaces with markets, live music and pop-ups in Centennial Square and the Inner Harbour is M51's own list — reinforced by "supported the return of major events like Symphony SPLASH!" and, on M52, the $175,000 Victoria Curling Club upgrade grant she co-sponsored with Coun. Dell (5 Apr 2026). Not Aligned: no arts and culture funding floor expressed per capita or as a share of operating expenditure with a 6-of-9 reduction lock (M50b), no extended civic-cultural hours or Sunday library hours (M50), no Royal Athletic Park restoration of the 2025 reallocation (M52). Distinct sentence from the /priorities OUR DWTN cleanliness line, which is row 26.

cells.what: local-tech procurement, open data, Wi-Fi, EV charging
trees, mode share, ecosystems, emergency preparedness

cells.quote: Voted with a unanimous council to "Initiate the process to hold a referendum to seek elector assent for the borrowing" of up to $168.9M for Crystal Pool (13 and 27 Jun 2024, CARRIED UNANIMOUSLY), to give the loan bylaw three readings (11 Jul 2024) and to adopt it (13 Mar 2025) after the 8 Feb 2025 assent vote passed at 58.71%. Not scored, deliberately: long-term borrowing requires elector assent by statute in BC, so this is compliance, not a chosen $25M rule — and she has stated no threshold, no 5-step sequence and no material-change rule. She is never individually named on any Crystal Pool division. Live tension: she is "researching and exploring options for a new central branch of the Greater Victoria Public Library", a new civic building with no threshold position attached.

14 Mar 2024, Review of Council Remuneration: the amendment that the raise "become effective after the next General Municipal Election" was defeated with her named opposed — "OPPOSED (5): Councillor Caradonna, Councillor Dell, Councillor Kim, Councillor Loughton, Councillor Thompson / DEFEATED (3 TO 5)". M79f is that rule verbatim in substance: "Any change to Council remuneration takes effect only at the start of the following term." She then voted for the 50%-of-mayor base, and on 15 Nov 2025 against scrapping the raises: "If we want councils that truly reflect our communities … then fair pay is essential." Shown in the same cell, cutting the other way, not a second mark: she voted for exploring a municipal lobbyist registry (11 Sep 2025, CARRIED 7 to 1, Hammond opposed, eight present) — an M79d hit; and she was the sole vote against requiring speakers at public hearings to disclose affiliation (2 Oct 2025, "OPPOSED (1): Councillor Loughton / CARRIED (7 to 1)"). No FOI-fee position (M79e); the 26 Feb 2026 FOI administration bylaw was unanimous and is not a fee waiver.

cells.what: neighbourhoods, language access, Local Area Plans
cells.quote: 3 Mar 2026, part 5.2 of the mayor's reallocation motion: "$100,000 to replenish the City's My Great Neighbourhood Grant program" — CARRIED UNANIMOUSLY, nine present.
cells.why: Commits, same instrument as M80, whose text is "expand the My Great Neighbourhood program". The campaign's own My Great Neighbourhood clause is used once only, on row 26, so it does not carry a second mark here. Not Aligned: no plain-language or French core-corpus standard (M80b), and no rolling Local Area Plan programme at two plans a year with parcel-level clarity (M80c). Counter-fact shown, not a mark: the neighbourhood-village structure she cites was delivered through "the adoption of Victoria 2050, the City's 10-year Official Community Plan update" — v1.10 explicitly declines the OCP repeal-and-replace route in favour of Local Area Plans, so that is a different instrument, not a second hit. "City of Communities" is branding; the Oaklands liaison seat is not a source.

cells.what: community surveys, turnout and ballot access
Saanich amalgamation (one line, not the whole topic)
cells.quote: We do not need another temperature check to know what the public wants. We need the structural framework to execute it, if that is what residents choose.
cells.why: Commits, and named in the 5-4 by two independent outlets: "Councillors Chris Coleman, Matt Dell, Krista Loughton and Susan Kim sided with the mayor" (25 Jun 2026). Comparable, not same: "no more temperature checks" maps onto M81's "Do not re-run the Assembly", and wanting the binding route maps onto M81's ask to the Province — "To come now with these restrictions is disrespectful to our electorate by shifting the goalposts for a binding referendum to a non-binding opinion poll". Missing: the joint financial, transitional and service-impact analysis commissioned with Saanich, publication against the Minister's conditions within 90 days, and the First Nations consultation the Minister named.
